newsitem.title: USA: Alfa sees 8 pct sales rise in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Alfa sees 8 pct sales rise in 1997.

text.p: Mexican conglomerate Grupo Industrial Alfa SA should see eight percent growth in sales next year, a senior company official said on Tuesday.
"We are optimistic about our prospects for 1997," Enrique Flores Rodriguez corporate vice president for communications told a Bear Stearns Investors Conference.
"We expect our consolidated sales volume to grow eight percent year-over-year."
The company's net sales for the first nine months of 1996 were about $2.6 billion.

Flores Rodriguez said among Alfa's four main subsidiaries, its Alpek petroleum chemical unit would see domestic sales increases of about nine percent in 1997; steelmaker Hylsamex eight percent; food processor Sigma Alimentos SA de CV 13 percent to $125 million; and the Versax autoparts and carpet unit should increase 23 percent to $200 million.
He also said Alfa would invest $2 billion in projects from 1996 to 2000 -- most of it in the first year of the plan.
Sixty percent of the spending already has been approved by the company's board of directors.
Flores Rodriquez said the company expected to generate most of its funding from internal revenues, with a "modest amount" from external financing.
Other possibilies for financing include an initial public offering for Alpek sales of equity at Hylsamex or issuing more Alfa stock.
The company is also exploring investments outside Mexico, especially in Central and South America.
However, he added, "we would not invest abroad just because we have money available."
